mainEntity.name: How Many Cases per Minute Can a Robotic Palletizer Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the platform. TRFCobot covers about 1 to 10 cases per minute, TRFCompact about 5 to 15 and TRFSpeed about 10 to 35. Lower-speed pharmaceutical lines fit the TRFCobot range. These are typical ranges for commercial screening: TRF confirms the final rate for your product, end-of-arm tool, pallet pattern and reach.

mainEntity.name: What Automation Reduces Labor Dependency in a Pharmaceutical Packaging Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Palletizing and case packing are usually the first steps to automate, because they are the most repetitive manual tasks after primary packaging. A cobot palletizer takes over case stacking, a case packer takes over grouping units into cases, and conveying removes manual carrying between them. Operators move to line supervision, quality checks and changeovers.

mainEntity.name: How Much Floor Space Does a Compact Palletizing Cell Require?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the pallet size, the number of pallet positions, how full pallets leave the cell and how operators reach it. TRFCobot and TRFCompact are designed as compact cells for plants where space at the end of the line is limited. TRF draws a layout with the cell, the infeed conveyor and operator access during the application review.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between an Integrated Case Packer and Separate Erecting, Packing and Sealing Machines?

acceptedAnswer.text: An integrated case packer erects the case, loads it and seals it in one coordinated machine. TRFOnepack works this way, with one controls platform, fewer interfaces and a smaller footprint than three separate machines connected by conveyors. Separate machines make sense when each step must be sized or replaced independently.

mainEntity.name: Can a Palletizer Be Integrated With My Existing Conveyor and Wrapping Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRFIntraflow supplies the accumulation, machine communication and palletizer interfaces that connect a new cell to the conveyors already installed, and TRFSpeed projects can include interfaces to wrapping, labeling and warehouse systems. The scope of each interface is defined during project engineering, so one partner is responsible for how the new cell fits the line.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for a Robotic Palletizer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the palletizer replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The payback calculator returns an initial estimate that a TRF Sales Engineer completes with your project costs.
